_meta.budget_mode: personal (sync_config.budget_mode; in shared mode the budget visibility rule is off)
_meta.dashboard_reads: once with events_limit=12, plus once per owner task category (household/school/repair) for urgentTasks and wallTasks; countdowns and events come from the first read
_meta.detail_documents_route: GET /documents/:id/thumbnail - same visibility lookup as preview/download, answers 415 for a non-DMS document without reading content; 415 = visible, 404 = not visible, 403 = refused, anything else fails the suite
_meta.detail_statuses: per route exactly three answers: its success status (200; thumbnail 415) = visible, 404 = not visible, 403 = refused; refusals next to visible rows stay in the cell as { visible, refused: { row: status } }
_meta.due_reminders: one due reminder per task, event and document row for each of these accounts (created_by = caller): admin, member, child, caregiver, member_none, split_guest, display; document_expiry rows are seeded directly like the others; token roles read the member's rows
_meta.health_delivery: due_reminders / medications is measured on the production path: one processDueMedications() run (medication-scheduler.js) after every other measurement, every seeded medication with one active 00:00 schedule, push spy, no channels; hearsOwnDose = the account received a push for a medication it owns, hearsCaredForDose = for one it does not own (n/a without a care grant); notLacksHealth = !lacksHealth(db, id) (cycle-reminders.js ~71). caregiver, member_none, split_guest and display own one private medication each so they can be addressed
_meta.health_unknown_account: unknown_account: the scheduler has no path for an id without a users row (owner and caregiver are foreign keys); recorded are the two exported production answers for such an id: recipientDeniedModulesIsNull (reminder-origins.js, null = drop the recipient) and notLacksHealth
_meta.mcp: list_tasks with include_future=true, list_upcoming_events with limit=100; the bridge calls call_api_operation with method GET and the /api/v1 path of each list route; a refused call is { status: tool_error, reason }
_meta.role_accounts: token_read / token_write / token_unscoped act for the member account
_meta.row_rules: row_rules holds the JavaScript row checks outside server/authorize (phase 2, B8a). Its rows are seeded AFTER every read path and the module level were measured and BEFORE the medication run (seedRowRules in the seed file); they are not in seed_counts and no read-path cell sees them. Blocks quick_links, task_writes, series and series_outlook_target are keyed by role (all ten), then by cell; outlook_classification is keyed by series. One cell = one leaf under a role (or one series in outlook_classification). Every block sends from its own client address 10.10.<role>.<block>; setup requests from 10.10.250.x
_meta.row_rules_cells: write cells are { ok, not_found, refused?: { row: { status, reason } } } over every seeded row of the block, or the one { status, reason } when the gate refused every row the same way. ok = the route's success status (or, where noted, the input check behind the rights check), not_found = its 404 with the route's own reason, refused = any 403; any other answer fails the suite
_meta.row_rules_display: the display writes like the wall: display cookie plus the session cookie and CSRF token its first GET below /api/v1 (GET /quick-links) handed out (csrfMiddleware keeps the token in req.session)
_meta.row_rules_outlook: series_outlook_target = the capabilities cell again after seedOutlookTarget: one outlook_accounts row (auto_sync_calendar_id, owner_user_id = member) with one outlook_calendar_selection row (enabled 1, can_edit 1); MS_CLIENT_ID / MS_CLIENT_SECRET / MS_REDIRECT_URI are pinned empty, so the sync tick returns before any request. outlook_classification = classifyLocalSeries (exported production function) per series before and after the target: the calendar answer shows eligibility only through can_override_occurrence
_meta.row_rules_quick_links: quicklink.<owner>.<all|private> for admin/member/child, seeded directly. list = GET /quick-links as { visible, editable (can_edit) }; overview / overview_household = the quicklinks row of GET /dashboard (personal, audience=household) in the same shape; change = PUT /quick-links/:id with {} (every field keeps its value, only updated_at moves), ok 200; remove = DELETE /quick-links/:id, ok 204, the row goes back with the same id and values after each 204; detail is n/a
_meta.row_rules_series: series.<owner>.<all|private|assignees> for admin/member/child: local, all-day, FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=3 from today+40 (all and assignees assigned to OTHER_OF[owner] via event_assignments), each with one linked occurrence on its second day created by its owner through PUT /calendar/:id/occurrences/:day. capabilities = GET /calendar over the series days as { visible, can_override (can_override_occurrence), can_detach (can_detach_occurrence) } per series. occurrence_put / occurrence_put_following / occurrence_delete / occurrence_delete_following / exceptions_post send the well-formed key of the day before the series start: ok = 400 invalid_recurrence_id, which baseOccurrenceFor() answers only AFTER visibility, ownership (not_owner) and isEligibleLocalSeries, so nothing is written ("past the checks"); exceptions_post computes the eligibility but only uses its reason for a series that is not locally owned. linked_put / linked_delete = PUT {} / DELETE on the linked occurrence row: ok = 400 calendar_occurrence_route_required (rejectLinkedOccurrenceResource, behind the same checks); not_found = 404 calendar_series_not_found / calendar_event_not_found
_meta.row_rules_task_writes: wtask.<owner>.<all|private|assignees> for admin/member/child (all and assignees assigned to OTHER_OF[owner] via task_assignments, description "- [ ] mx item", no due date), plus wtask.admin.assignees.display assigned to the display account (not a realistic state: without it the display branch of PATCH /:id/status, tasks.js ~2287, answers for no task because mayAccessTask runs first). One cell per mayAccessTask call site: completions = GET /:id/completions (~2604), check = PATCH /:id/check {line 0, checked false} (~2471, unchanged line, no write), archive = PATCH /:id/archive {archived false} (~2418), status = PATCH /:id/status {status open} on an open task (~2244, then the display branch ~2287), subtask = POST /tasks {title, parent_task_id} (~1399, ok 201, the subtask is deleted), remove = DELETE /:id (~2529, the row and its assignments go back with the same id). next_due_date = PATCH /:id/status {status done} on wtask.chain.origin (shared, weekly) whose followup wtask.chain.followup (admin, private) already exists: next names the followup when the answer carries its due date, null otherwise (nextDueDateAfter ~1860: display reads visibility all, people mayAccessTask); the display names done_by_user_id = admin; the origin is reopened and its completion row deleted after each 200
_meta.seed_shape: tasks and events per owner all/private/assignees (all and assignees assigned to one other account via the assignment table, legacy assigned_to NULL); task.admin.private.legacy-assigned-member sets only tasks.assigned_to = member; task.admin.assignees.secondary-member is not seeded because task.admin.assignees already is "assignment row only"; event.member.ics-unshared / ics-shared come from two subscriptions of the member; countdown flag on task.member.assignees and event.member.assignees; document expiry (today+10, lead 30 days) on the member's three documents and on document.admin.private; tasks due today, events all-day in two days, budget entries today
_meta.tokens: minted via POST /auth/api-tokens with subject_user_id = member: {"token_read":"19 scopes, every module read","token_write":"19 scopes, every module write","token_unscoped":"scopes NULL"}
